design_rationale:
WORKLOG task 1 (debt_waivers_disputes_and_repayment), frozen_time 2026-10-05.

[Step 0 draw] draw_counts.py --task 1 -> {"prerequisite_problems": 2, "factor_counts": [6, 4, 4]}. Assignment: compromise offer (root) 6, reduced-withholding proposal 4, approved reduced withholding 4.

[Scope snapshot] Occupied by task 0: debt_ext_plan_reinstatement_deposit, debt_ext_waiver_request_amount, debt_ext_plan_request_term, debt_ext_plan_installment and their four tools (direct-payment plan family on a compensation overpayment). Claimed here: debt_ext_reduced_withholding_proposal (record_reduced_withholding_request_043db99b, agent, debt_repayment_plan_requested kind reduced_withholding), debt_ext_reduced_withholding_amount (start_reduced_withholding_20dc00ef, agent, debt_plan_started benefit_withholding), debt_ext_compromise_offer_amount (submit_compromise_offer_8c2d0269, owner user, debt_compromise_offered). Together the two tasks cover all seven extended policies; scopes and tools are disjoint. Last task: nothing is left unclaimed.

[Why a good test] The caller, an 80-year-old pensioner whose whole pension is being withheld, asks only to settle his Veterans Pension Overpayment for less with a lump sum. The compromise rule, for a debtor whose benefit payments are being withheld for the debt, values the offer from an approved reduced monthly withholding ('For a debtor whose VA benefit payments are being withheld for the debt, the lump sum a compromise offer puts forward is worked out only after the debt carries an approved reduced monthly withholding from the debtor's benefit payments.'), and the withholding rule waits on a reduced-withholding request dated today ('Reduced withholding does not start on a debt until the debt carries a reduced-withholding request received on the day it starts.'). The agent must discover both hops from the rules, set up the withholding on his behalf, and only then hand him the offer. Breadth: the debt ledger (offsets, waiver request with report, denial), date spans (notice age, three/six/twelve-month windows), and the pension difficulty's records (award category, net worth, countable income, monthly payments and their withholding, rate adjustments).

[Problem-tree card] root debt_ext_compromise_offer_amount.
 edge 1: compromise -> approved reduced withholding, value_input, gate monthly_withholding, form state (affirmative 'only after'). Only start_reduced_withholding_20dc00ef sets a benefit-withholding amount (the task 0 plan start sets direct_payment). False at opening: debt status active, method none, amount 0.0. Skip effect: 885.65 -> 0.00.
 edge 2: approved reduced withholding -> proposal, value_input, gate proposal, form state (negated 'does not start until'). Only record_reduced_withholding_request_043db99b writes a reduced-withholding request. False at opening: the only requests are the waiver request and its denial. Skip effect: 37.05 -> 25.00.
 Four-point test: ordering connective present; record-visible state; no tool, id or code token; strength matches the condition. Order: proposal, withholding, offer (a chain). The customer's own write: the compromise offer.

[Base-invariant card] Step 9 (debt_repayment_plan_requested): debt_evt_repayment_plan.plan_on_active_debt - status active -> satisfied. Step 11 (debt_plan_started): debt_evt_repayment_plan policy_scope; reduced withholding requires a Financial Status Report - the 2026-05-20 waiver request carried one. Step 13 (debt_compromise_offered): debt_evt_compromise policy_scope (its authority gate applies to the decision, balance 5670.00 is far below 100000.00); debt_excl_single_pending_request.no_undecided_request - the waiver request is decided (denial 2026-08-25 cites it) -> satisfied. No time gate applies to these subjects.

[Business-object card] Target: the Veterans Pension Overpayment created by the 2026-03-04 rate adjustment (Social Security of 4800.00 a year counted from 2023-12-01; 27 months x 400.00 = 10800.00). Rows in the aggregates: five offsets of 1026.00 (2026-06-01, 07-01, 07-31, 09-01, 10-01) each tied to its pension payment; the waiver request (with report) and its denial. Excluded: the February to May pension payments (not withheld; May 1 precedes the 30-day offset start).

[Factor card]
 proposal: starting_figure method pension multi-source -> 102.60 (baseline 94.50, result 57.84); care_pct pension -> 80 (78.49); offset_pct -> 90 (69.77); denial_pct multi-source -> 85 (73.88). Fall-back 94.50. Near-miss: the February payment of 1426.00 is not the latest payment.
 withholding: approved_figure method pension multi-source -> 47.10 (baseline 62.80, 49.40); assets_pct pension -> 90 (41.17); income_pct pension -> 92 (40.28); history_pct -> 95 (39.00). Fall-back 62.80. Near-miss: the 2026-07-01 payment is outside the three-month window (MONTHS = 3).
 compromise: recovery_months pension -> 36 (baseline 60, 1393.65); recovery_value method -> present value 1217.871 (baseline 1333.80, 969.95); cost_pct -> 2 (baseline standard 5, 858.54); hardship_pct -> 90 (984.05); rate_cut_pct pension history -> 85 (1041.94); notice_pct -> 97 (913.04). Fall-back 2111.85. Near-miss: the February income match created no overpayment; only the March rate adjustment counts.

[Seed rows] customer; pension award (Housebound, income 9000.00, net worth 21400.00); nine monthly pension payments (February 1426.00, March onward 1026.00, June onward withheld in full); income match and rate adjustment reports; the debt; five offsets; waiver request and denial. Each feeds a factor listed above; removing the pension award moves every pension factor to its fall-through.

[Persona] Harold W. Brenneman, slow and courteous, writes numbers down. Volunteers only the goal (settle for less with a lump sum, the whole pension is being kept). Gives phone 4125550192, then SSN 5603, VA file 358204417, DOB 1946-02-11 when asked. Passive: lets the representative set up whatever is needed first; submits the offer with his Financial Status Report when handed it; reads the amount back and ends.

[Standard solution] Locate, verify, read debt, transactions, requests, pension award, pension payments, income reports; (9) record the reduced-withholding request 62.80; (11) start reduced withholding 37.05 from 2026-11; (13) hand over the compromise offer 885.65 with a report, outside the hold window.

[Verification run] Handling-time recomputation replaying the gold writes: proposal 62.80 (fall-back 94.50), withholding 37.05 (62.80), offer 885.65 (fall-back 2111.85 after the round-2 standard 5 percent cost of collection; it was 2223.00 before that change). Skips: step 9 -> 25.00; step 11 -> 654.49. Gates run per task: check_extended, check_task_tools, replay_tasks, check_solvability, check_compute, check_grounding, check_cache_diff, check_cross_fire.

[Draft recomputation from the visible context] The compromise rule names the approved reduced withholding it waits on; the withholding rule names the request it waits on; the records show an active debt with no plan and no reduced-withholding request. Applying the published ladders to the records reproduces 62.80, 37.05 and 885.65.

[Rework round 2, audit policy_task/debt_waivers_disputes_and_repayment]
G2 symptom: the compromise gate on an approved reduced withholding bound every offer, including debtors with no benefit to withhold from (lump sum 0.00), contradicting base 'A debtor may offer a lump sum smaller than the balance'. Change: the prerequisite sentence is now conditional ('For a debtor whose VA benefit payments are being withheld for the debt, ...'), the rule says a debtor not collected by withholding may offer at any time, the base sentence is declared in overwrite, and the monthly amount falls back to the recorded plan installment or the smallest plan installment instead of 0. Re-run: gold unchanged at 885.65; skip of step 11 now gives 654.49.
G3 symptom: the proposal's starting figure read the latest pension payment of any award, while the rule requires a running pension. Change: pension_payment is 0 unless the pension award's status is running. No change on this world (running).
G6 symptom: recovery_value's 'months at least 24' conjunct was universal and its fall-through unreachable. Change: the ladder now splits by how recovery would be collected: approved benefit withholding and balance >= 5000 -> present value; direct-payment plan and balance >= 5000 -> 15 percent direct-plan discount; otherwise undiscounted (reachable for billed or small debts). discount_months_min removed. Tier taken unchanged; 969.95 sensitivity unchanged.
G7 symptom: 'not referred to Treasury' was universal and the 1-2 offset fall-through got zero cost. Change: cost tiers are 3+ offsets in three months -> 2, none -> 10, otherwise (1-2) the standard cost 5, which is now part of the baseline. Re-run: cost baseline 858.54, whole fall-back 2111.85, gold 885.65.
Finding 4: '37.0476' corrected to 37.04886 in factor_trace and tracing (result 37.05 unchanged). T1-O1: single-row conditions no longer labelled multi-source.


[Rework round 3, audit revision_2]
R2-G8 symptom: the round-2 sentence 'A debtor whose debt is not being collected by withholding from VA benefit payments may offer such a lump sum at any time.' granted a timeless permission that base forbids for referred debts ('Once referred, VA no longer ... takes compromise offers') and for a debt with an undecided waiver, dispute or compromise (single pending request). Change: the sentence now reads '... is not held to the reduced-withholding step below; every other condition on taking an offer still applies to that debtor.' It only scopes the conditional gate and grants nothing, so every inherited base condition stands. No compute change; gold 885.65, skip effects 25.00 / 654.49 and fall-back 2111.85 unchanged on this world (pension withheld, not referred, no pending request).
R2-T1 symptom: the [Verification run] line still quoted the round-1 fall-back 2223.00. Change: corrected to 2111.85 (37.05 x 60 x 0.95), matching computations[2].baseline_result.
user_scenario:
You are Harold W. Brenneman, an 80-year-old Navy veteran of the Vietnam era who lives alone in a small house outside Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. You are courteous, a bit hard of hearing, and you take things slowly; you have a notepad and you like to write numbers down. You receive a Veterans Pension, and in the spring VA told you that you had been overpaid because your Social Security had not been counted. You asked VA by mail to forgive that debt and they turned you down in August. Since June they have been keeping my whole pension check, as you put it, and you are getting by on your Social Security alone. Your son Mark has offered to lend you some money, so what you want from this call is to settle this debt for less with a lump sum: you want to put in an offer to VA today, and you want the representative to tell you what amount to offer.

You start by saying you are calling about the pension overpayment debt, that VA has been keeping my whole pension check, and that you would like to settle this debt for less with a lump sum your son can help with. When asked how to find you, you give your phone number, 4125550192. When asked to confirm your identity, you give the last four of your Social Security number, 5603, then your VA file number, 358204417, then your date of birth, 1946-02-11, one at a time and slowly. You do not know internal reference numbers. If asked what you owe, you say you are not sure, a few thousand dollars at least, and you would rather they look it up. If asked how much your son could put up, you say he told you he could manage up to about fifteen hundred dollars. If asked about other income, you say your Social Security is your only other income and nothing has changed since VA looked at it.

You do not know VA's rules and you do not propose steps. If the representative explains that something has to be set up on your account before the offer can be worked out, you tell them that is fine and to go ahead and do it for you. When the representative tells you the amount to offer and hands the offer over to you to submit, you sign and submit it exactly as they set it up, with your Financial Status Report attached, because you still have the copy you filled out for your waiver request and nothing in it has changed. You do not argue with the figures; you ask the representative to repeat each one slowly so you can write it down.

Once the representative tells you the offer has been submitted and gives you the amount, you read the amount back, thank them, and say goodbye. If the representative says an offer cannot be taken, you ask once why, write down what they say, and end the call politely.

edges.condition: Where benefit offsets are being taken on the debt, the debt is in repayment-plan status with benefit withholding as the method and an approved monthly withholding recorded on it; a debt not collected by benefit offset needs none.
edges.policy_source: For a debtor whose VA benefit payments are being withheld for the debt, the lump sum a compromise offer puts forward is worked out only after the debt carries an approved reduced monthly withholding from the debtor's benefit payments.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: The debt is in active collection with no plan: no benefit-withholding method and no approved monthly withholding.
unresolved_at_frozen_time.flips_to_true_by: Step 11 sets status repayment_plan, method benefit_withholding, monthly amount 37.05.

edges.condition: The latest reduced-withholding request on the debt is dated the day the withholding starts and states the monthly withholding proposed.
edges.policy_source: Reduced withholding does not start on a debt until the debt carries a reduced-withholding request received on the day it starts.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: The debt's only requests are the waiver request and its denial; no reduced-withholding request exists.
unresolved_at_frozen_time.flips_to_true_by: Step 9 records a reduced-withholding request dated 2026-10-05 proposing 62.80.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: A chain: compromise lump sum <- approved reduced withholding <- reduced-withholding request. No problem has two prerequisites, so nothing can be reordered; each write must follow the one whose value it reads.

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Skipping step 11: no reduced withholding is recorded, so the monthly amount falls to the 25.00 smallest plan installment valued undiscounted over 36 months, and requested_amount becomes 654.49 instead of 885.65; the debt also stays active instead of repayment_plan.
Skipping step 9: no proposal, the approved figure is 0 and monthly_amount falls to the 25.00 floor instead of 37.05.

prerequisite_closure.no_user_hint: user_scenario asks only to settle the debt for less with a lump sum and complains that the whole pension check is being kept. It never mentions reduced withholding, a withholding request or any policy id; the only related line is passive: if the representative explains something has to be set up first, he lets them go ahead.
prerequisite_closure.tools_do_not_block: task_tools.py: submit_compromise_offer_8c2d0269 only creates the offer row; start_reduced_withholding_20dc00ef only updates status, method, amount and start month; record_reduced_withholding_request_043db99b only creates the request row. None reads another request or the debt's status and none returns an error, so each writes faithfully even when its prerequisite is unresolved.
